title: レアアースなど重要鉱物開発、日豪が6事業を優先指定　首脳合意へ
extracted_text:
日豪両政府がレアアース（希土類）やニッケルなどの6つの開発案件を優先事業に指定することが1日、分かった。オーストラリアでの開発にかかる許認可手続きなどを迅速に進めてもらいやすくなる。中国への依存度が高い重要物資を中心に供給網の多角化を急ぐ。

高市早苗首相が4日、豪州でアルバニージー首相と会談して確認する見通しだ。両首相は重要鉱物を経済安全保障関係の中核に格上げすることで合意し、共同声明を発出する。

6つある優先事業のうちレアアースの生産は 双日 とエネルギー・金属鉱物資源機構（JOGMEC）との共同出資会社が手掛ける。2025年から中国への依存度が特に高い重希土類の日本向け供給を始めた。

住友金属鉱山 や 三菱商事 などが共同保有するニッケル事業も対象とする。双日が出資するガリウム回収の案件や、JX金属と 丸紅 が参画するレアアースなどを含むミネラルサンド（砂状鉱物）開発も含まれる。

豪州政府は26年4月に資源開発の認可を早める制度改革を発表しており、手続きの迅速化に向けた環境は整いつつある。これまでは連邦・州政府それぞれが審査・承認して時間を要する例が目立っていたものの、国家環境基準を設けて州政府が連邦に代わって環境審査や承認を担う。

豪州政府が25年に立ち上げた重要鉱物戦略備蓄制度も活用する。12億豪ドル（約1400億円）を投じ、戦略的に重要な鉱物の安定供給を確保する仕組みだ。

鉱物開発プロジェクトは探査から生産開始まで10年以上かかることもあり、価格変動のリスクも高い。長期投資の採算性と事業の安定性を支えれば長期購入者を確保しやすくなる。

重要鉱物は蓄電池やモーター、半導体などの製造に不可欠だ。経済産業省によるとレアアースの6〜7割ほどを中国から輸入する。輸出制限やシーレーン（海上交通路）の封鎖に対して脆弱との指摘があった。

中東情勢で浮き彫りになった原油などのエネルギー安保でも協力を打ち出す。

日本は豪州に軽油やガソリンなどの石油製品を輸出し、豪州から液化天然ガス（LNG）や石炭を輸入している。両首相はエネルギー安保に関する共同声明をまとめ、これらの物資を相互に融通し続ける方針で合意する。

中国の動きや中東情勢を念頭に「正当性のない輸出入規制に対処する」と強調する。

translated_text:
It was learned on the 1st that the Japanese and Australian governments have designated six development projects—including rare earths (lanthanides) and nickel—as priority projects. This is expected to streamline and accelerate permitting processes for development in Australia. The two countries are rushing to diversify their supply chains, focusing on critical materials for which they are highly dependent on China.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is expected to meet with Prime Minister Albanese in Australia on the 4th to confirm these arrangements. The two leaders are set to agree to elevate critical minerals to the core of their economic security relationship and issue a joint statement.

Among the six priority projects, rare earth production will be handled by a joint venture between Sojitz and the Japan Oil, Gas and Metals National Corporation (JOGMEC). Starting in 2025, the company began supplying heavy rare earths—materials for which dependence on China is particularly high—to Japan.

A nickel project jointly held by Sumitomo Metal Mining, Mitsubishi Corporation and others is also included. Also covered are a gallium recovery project in which Sojitz invests, and mineral sand (granular mineral) development involving rare earths in which JX Nippon Mining & Metals and Marubeni participate.

The Australian government announced a regulatory reform in April this year to accelerate resource development permitting, creating an environment conducive to faster procedures. Previously, reviews and approvals by both federal and state governments had often been time-consuming. Now, national environmental standards are being established, with state governments handling environmental reviews and approvals on behalf of the federal government.

Australia's Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve system, launched in 2025, will also be utilized. The system is designed to ensure stable supply of strategically critical minerals by investing 12 billion Australian dollars (approximately 140 billion yen).

Mineral development projects can take more than 10 years from exploration to production, with high price fluctuation risks. By supporting the profitability of long-term investments and business stability, it will become easier to secure long-term buyers.

Critical minerals are indispensable for manufacturing batteries, motors, and semiconductors. According to the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan imports about 60–70% of its rare earths from China. There have been concerns about vulnerability to export restrictions and the possibility of sea lane (maritime route) blockages.

Cooperation will also be announced for energy security—including crude oil, highlighted by the situation in the Middle East.

Japan exports petroleum products such as diesel and gasoline to Australia, while importing liquefied natural gas (LNG) and coal from Australia. The two prime ministers will compile a joint statement on energy security and agree to continue mutually exchanging these materials.

With China's actions and the Middle East situation in mind, they will emphasize working together to "address unjustified export and import restrictions."
title_en: Japan and Australia Designate Six Projects as Priority for Critical Mineral Development Including Rare Earths; Leaders Set to Agree
